The core mathematical operation involves calculating the gradient between the Layer 1 consensus and the Layer 2 adjusted fair value. This governing rule functions as a strict inequality constraint: unless the absolute difference between the model's posterior and the market's prior exceeds a predefined confidence interval, the system defaults to zero action. This prevents overfitting to noisy situational data and enforces capital preservation. The entire framework operates as a continuous feedback loop, where live line movements and injury updates continuously re-normalize the Layer 1 baseline, requiring constant re-evaluation of the Layer 2 perturbations to identify genuine, non-collinear edges.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive lineage traces back to the Efficient Market Hypothesis, adapted through modern sports analytics. It borrows heavily from quantum mechanical perturbation theory, where a stable baseline state is altered by external stressors. Historically, it evolves from basic moneyline arbitrage into a sophisticated, multi-layered Bayesian inference engine that respects market wisdom while exploiting granular, physical tracking data to find micro-inefficiencies in real-time.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the opposing agents—primarily the sharp money syndicates and algorithmic market makers—as hyper-rational actors who instantly price in public narrative. Their 'mind' is represented by the Layer 1 consensus. Simultaneously, we model the on-field coaches and quarterbacks as constrained optimizers reacting to immediate physical threats. A quarterback facing a 12.0 pressure rate will mentally abandon complex progressions, collapsing their decision tree. Our engine anticipates these psychological and physical collapses, predicting how human actors will deviate from optimal scripts under duress.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The cross-layer veto is the critical anti-collinearity filter. It ensures that our Layer 2 trench signals are not merely echoing what the market has already priced in. If the market moves the line because of a known injury to a starting tackle, our Layer 2 pressure metrics will reflect that same reality. The veto detects this collinearity and forces a 'PASS', preventing us from betting against a move that is already fully justified by the new Layer 1 equilibrium. True alpha only exists when Layer 2 reveals a hidden structural advantage the broader market has yet to digest.
